test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 22 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In which of the following years did Lord Curzon announce the partition of Bengal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1905**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Lord Curzon, the then Viceroy of India, announced the **Partition of Bengal** on **July 19, 1905**, and it was implemented on **October 16, 1905**.
 
• The partition was aimed at dividing Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam**, with a Muslim majority, and **West Bengal**, with a Hindu majority.
 
• The official reason given was to improve administrative efficiency in the large and populous Bengal province, which had a population of over 78 million at the time.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and marked the beginning of the **Swadeshi Movement** (1905-1911), a significant phase in India's struggle for independence.
 
• Due to severe opposition and unrest, the partition was annulled in **1911** by the British government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swadeshi Movement:**

 
 
• Launched in response to the Partition of Bengal, this movement emphasized the use of indigenous goods and boycotting British products.
 
• It saw the rise of nationalist leaders like **Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, and Lala Lajpat Rai**.
 
• Key cultural aspects, such as nationalistic songs like *"Vande Mataram,"* became symbols of resistance.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Challenges:**
 
 
• Bengal was the largest province in British India, making governance difficult, which was cited as the primary reason for partition.
 
• However, critics argued that the real motive was to create religious division and weaken the growing nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• **Reversal of Partition:**
 
 
• In 1911, the British annulled the partition due to the sustained opposition and shifted the capital of British India from **Calcutta to Delhi**.
 
• The annulment is considered a partial victory for Indian nationalists, though it did not eliminate British control.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Nationalism:**
 
 
• The partition and subsequent unrest significantly contributed to the growth of the Indian National Congress and the demand for **Swaraj (self-rule)**.
 
• It also led to the unification of Indian leaders across regions and religions to oppose British policies.
